name: Andrew O'Donnell
headline: CLINICAL RESEARCH COORDINATOR
summary: Clinical Research Coordinator with 8+ years of experience across Stanford University School of Medicine, the U.S. Air Force, and a Level I trauma center. Coordinated concurrent NIH and industry clinical trials (Phase II-IV) for 1,500+ participants, with direct experience in informed consent, eligibility screening, study visits, safety reporting with CTCAE grading, and EDC data management under ICH GCP and 21 CFR. Licensed CPT-I phlebotomist with DOT specimen shipping certification and bedside emergency department experience caring for pediatric hematology and oncology patients. ACRP-Certified Project Manager and Certified Professional.

Clinical Research Coordinator Associate | Stanford University Department of Medicine, Palo Alto, CA | Nov 2021 - Feb 2026

Executed clinical operations for 1,500+ participants across concurrent NIH and industry trials (Phase II-IV) in infectious disease, post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2, and chronic diseases; led recruitment and enrollment operations with the site consistently ranked among the top enrollment sites nationally.

Conducted patient-facing study visits onsite and through decentralized workflows, including eConsent, telehealth check-ins, ePRO, and home investigational product shipments, ensuring protocol adherence and participant engagement.
Maintained protocol compliance and safety documentation, including AE/SAE reporting with CTCAE grading, partnering with sponsors, CROs, and PIs to sustain audit readiness under ICH GCP and 21 CFR.

Served as Honest Broker for Gilead GS-US-685-6819, ensuring HIPAA-compliant consent and data handling in direct collaboration with trial leadership; involved in budgeting, billing, and feasibility management.
Optimized REDCap/OnCore databases with validation rules, queries, and dashboards, achieving 90%+ on-time query resolution.

Trained and onboarded incoming clinical research coordinators on protocol workflows, eConsent, ePRO, and REDCap/OnCore data entry; developed study-specific training materials and acted as the escalation point for study procedures.
Technical Operations Manager (Contract) | International SOS (Iqarus), Fort Lee, VA | Aug 2021 - Sep 2021
Led biomedical operations at the first U.S. haven site for Operation Allies Welcome, supporting medical intake and care for 25K+ evacuees from Afghanistan.

Designed and implemented high-throughput COVID-19 testing and vaccination protocols that cut average processing time per patient from 30 to approximately 18 minutes (40% faster), and trained staff and interagency partners on the resulting workflows.
Collaborated with Army Public Health and interagency partners to ensure rapid benefit enrollment, offsite medical referrals, and 100% compliance with CDC vaccination and screening requirements.
Emergency Department Technician | RCET | Children's Hospital of Orange County, Santa Ana, CA | Jan 2018 - Oct 2021
Delivered frontline care in a top-ranked Level I pediatric trauma center, assisting in triage, stabilization, and 20K+ annual emergency encounters.

Provided bedside care for pediatric hematology and oncology patients, including fever and neutropenia presentations and oncology code events; prepared sterile fields and supplies for implanted port access.
Assisted in code events, including intubation, resuscitation, medication preparation, and patient transport, as an extension of physicians and nurses.
Precepted and trained new emergency department technicians on triage support, trauma bay setup, and respiratory equipment operation.
Sustained reliability of respiratory care equipment (CPAP, BiPAP, ventilators, high-flow O2) through proactive maintenance and troubleshooting.
Healthcare Technology Manager | 4A2x5 | U.S. Air Force, Various Locations | Sep 2017 - Sep 2025, ADT - Reserve
Maintained 98%+ preventive-maintenance compliance across 200+ biomedical devices valued at $2M+, ensuring Joint Commission and DoD accreditation readiness.
Led HTM for the 752nd Medical Squadron during Global Medic 2019, supervising 6 biomedical personnel in a multinational mass-casualty exercise.
Supervised and trained airmen in biomedical equipment maintenance and safe equipment use, achieving zero equipment-related incidents.
